content.comment_body: Good morning, We have several expanded units from an older programmable relay and want to upgrade to the most recent version. Q1: Are the older input/output expansion units compatible with newer hardware? Q2: If I purchase updated software and use the old connection cable, can I retrieve the previous program and install it onto the new device? Q3: Is it possible to transfer programs between devices in CSV format? Any assistance on these topics would be greatly appreciated.

For Q1: How do you define 'old'? Hardware from around 2014 is considered new. Expansion modules with certain article numbers at the end are not compatible with the newer hardware versions. The new expansion modules have different article numbers ending in another sequence. You can check this in the official product notes: [document]. The latest base modules are on version [version_no]. The software version is also the latest release. For Q2: Older programs can be used with new versions, but the hardware type must be changed in the software for successful installation, for example from an older type to the most recent version. For Q3: I'm not sure what you mean by transferring programs in CSV format.
The base module is on version [version_no] and the expansion module is on article number [article_no]. Based on the drawings, I estimate the equipment dates to around 2004.
I hope you've reviewed the product note linked above. This clarifies that you'll require updated base modules as well as new expansion modules for compatibility.

analysis.insight_summary: Users aim to upgrade older programmable relay systems to the latest hardware and software. Key challenges include hardware incompatibility between legacy and newer expansion modules, uncertainty in how programs can be migrated, and questions about data format support during transfers. The absence of backward compatibility for older components raises concerns about continued use and support for legacy equipment.
analysis.user_expectations: Users anticipate that new hardware will be compatible with existing expansion modules, that program extraction and deployment using the updated software and original cables will be straightforward, and that there will be support for migrating programs through interoperable formats like CSV.
